Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle. Quezon City http: Ifwww. dilg .gov.ph 31 JUL 2010 DILG OPINION NO. 40 MAYOR JUNARD Q. CHAN Office of the Mayor Lapu-Lapu City Dear Mayor Chan: s. 202. This has reference to your lecter dated 5 July 2019, requesting the Department's legal opinion on the validity of Lapu-Lapu City Ordinance No. 14- 200-2019, entitled "AN ORDINANCE PROVIDING AN OFFICE SPACE AT THE LAPU- LAPU CITY HALL AS DISTRICT OFFICE OF THE MEMBER OF THE HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVE FOR THE LONE CONGRESSIONAL DISTRICT OF LAPU-LAPU CITY". At the outset, perusal of the subject ordinance, appears that the same suffers from legal infirmities. Primarily, the same fails to comply with Section 59(d) of the Local Government Code, pursuant to the Certification (attached as Annex "D") dated 2 July, 2019 issued by the Secretary of the Sangguniang Panlungsod, Mr. Francisco Y. Limpangug, to wit: "SECTION 59. Effectivity of Ordinances or Resolutions. (d) In the case of highly urbanized cities, the main features of the ordinance or resolution duly enacted or adopted shall, in addition to being posted, be published once in a local newspaper of general circulation within the city: Provided, That in the absence thereof the ordinance or resolution shall be published in any newspaper of general circulation. " This Department is of considered view that the subject ordinance is not yet effective as it has not yet been published in accordance with the afore-quoted provision of the LGC. Secondly, the power to allocate and assign office in the City Hall belongs to the Mayor and not to the Sanggunian. Pursuant to Section 455(b)(ix) of the LGC, the Mayor shall allocate and assign office space to city and other officials who by law or ordinance are entitled to such space in city hall and other buildings owned or leased by the city government. The law is very clear that the power to allocate and assign office space should be exercised by the Mayor, not by the Sanggunian, and should cover officials and employees of the city government only. Also, it should be by authority of law or an ordinance. In this case, since the ordinance is ineffective, the same should not be the basis for allocation of the said space.

Obviously, it is a clear case of a midnight ordinance considering the circumstance that it was passed last June or shortly before the end of the former Mayor's term, and its design to favor the former Mayor who is now the sitting congresswoman. Worst, the ordinance will deprive the newly elected Mayor of his power to allocate office spaces to city officials and employees. Accordingly, for an ordinance to be valid and effective, the same should not violate the Constitution and existing laws, such as the LGC. For clearly ignoring Sections 59(d) and 455(b)(ix) of the LGC, this Department believes that the subject ordinance is ineffective and invalid, therefore, should not be implemented. We hope we have assisted you on the matter. Very truly yours, By Authority of the Secretary: MARI L C. SACENDONCILLO, CESO 111 Undersecretary CC: Dir. Leocadio T. Trovela Regional Director DILG-Region VII
